session_cue.text: Sir Phidipaldi slapping the Reeve with his glove

previous.text: The party reached Brandonsford at sunset, following a treasure map to places they did not recognize.
Reginald the frog warned the party to avoid the Clurichen, a trickster that roams town each night.
Eric the Reeve offered a bounty on the black dragon that took woodsman George's arm. Sir Phidipaldi then insulted Eric and slapped him with a glove.
Lady Hilda offered to join the party on the dragon hunt for pay.
The thief Drop Dead Ned offered himself and his killer wasp for hire at 100 gold a week.
Bentley and Farmer Gill told the party that supplies have stopped reaching Brandonsford.
Sir Phidipaldi struck a deal with Quinn to get back at Bentley, whom Quinn blames for his vanishing ale.

current.where_you_are: Sir Phidipaldi is in the empty Golden Egg Tavern with its owner, Quinn. Wayman Tisdale and Dr. Uriah are across the street in the Clumsy Fox Tavern. Dunk is at Farmer Gill's farm, drinking with Gill on the porch and planning to sleep in the barn.

Your goals.text: Find the treasure shown on the party's treasure map.
The party is considering killing the black dragon and dragging its body into town for Eric the Reeve's 1000 gold.
Dunk is considering acquiring Farmer Gill's prize mule, Shamus. Gill says it would let Dunk start his own farm.

What could help.text: If the party pays Lady Hilda, she will join them on the dragon hunt.
Lady Hilda has chain mail and a shield but says she cannot kill the dragon herself. She has named no fee.
If Dunk pays Farmer Gill 100 gold, Gill will sell him Shamus.
If Dunk helps kill the dragon, Gill might give him Shamus, though Gill never agreed to that trade.

Still unanswered.text: What empties or knocks over Quinn's stock every night?
What is the Clurichen doing in Brandonsford each night?
Why have no goods reached Brandonsford in months?

Promises and debts.text: Quinn will pay Sir Phidipaldi 100 gold for helping him get back at Bentley.
Sir Phidipaldi must stage a showy fake ale delivery of water-filled bottles at the Golden Egg with Quinn.

threads.name: The treasure map
threads.note: The party is following a treasure map whose marked locations they do not recognize; the treasure is still unfound.

threads.name: The Clurichen trickster
threads.note: Reginald warned that a trickster called a Clurichen comes from the riverbanks into town every night up to no good, an open danger and question.

threads.name: The dragon and Eric the Reeve's bounty
threads.note: Eric offered 1000 gold for killing the black dragon and dragging its body into town (beat_18), and the rumours, George's encounter, Gill's sighting and his sons' hunt all bear on this one dragon. Sir Phidipaldi's insult and duel challenge to Eric (beat_20, beat_21) strained relations with the bounty-giver but did not end the offer.

threads.name: Lady Hilda's offer to join the party
threads.note: Lady Hilda said she cannot kill the dragon herself but would join adventurers for money, and Sir Phidipaldi said they would talk to the Reeve and come back for her services; her stated purpose ties her to the dragon hunt.

threads.name: Drop Dead Ned's offer of hire
threads.note: The thief Drop Dead Ned offered himself and his killer wasp for 100 gold a week, with a per-kill rebate, and Dr. Uriah said he would think about it.

threads.name: Brandonsford's missing shipment
threads.note: The town's restocking shipment is a week overdue and goods have not reached town in months; nobody has yet gone after it.

threads.name: Farmer Gill's mule Shamus
threads.note: Gill offered Dunk the mule for 100 gold; Dunk asked to trade work, Gill pointed to killing the dragon, and Dunk is sleeping on the offer with no deal settled.

threads.name: Warwick's mithril chain shirt
threads.note: Warwick the increasingly paranoid smith displays a superb mithril chain shirt he refuses to sell, an item the party may want.

threads.name: Quinn's deal against Bentley
threads.note: Quinn's stock vanishes nightly and he blames Bentley; Sir Phidipaldi agreed to help get back at Bentley for 100 gold and to stage a fake ale delivery. The mystery of the vanishing stock bears directly on this deal, so it is one situation.

facts.text: Find the treasure shown on the party's treasure map.
Where are the locations marked on the treasure map, and which of them holds the treasure?

classification.grounding_justification: The beat explicitly states the party does not recognize the map's marked locations and only assumes the treasure is in one of them.
classification.investigative_depth_justification: Identifying places on a map is mostly a matter of locating them; little hidden circumstance is suggested.
classification.narrative_payoff_justification: The answer is mainly instrumental to finding the treasure.
classification.investigative_potential_justification: Locals in Brandonsford and exploration of the unknown surrounding land could plausibly be used to identify the marks.

facts.text: Reginald the Frog warns that a little trickster called a Clurichen comes from the riverbanks into Brandonsford every night, up to no good, and that the party should stay away from wherever it goes.

classification.negative_outcome_clarity_justification: The Clurichen is only said to be up to no good; no particular harm is named.
classification.outcome_severity_justification: Nothing suggests more than trickery or minor mischief.
classification.evidentiary_strength_justification: Rests on the testimony of a single talking frog, a local but unverified source.
classification.evidence_of_progression_justification: Reginald describes a nightly recurring pattern of the Clurichen entering town.
classification.preventability_justification: The party can heed the warning and avoid where it goes, but has no known means to stop it.

facts.text: What is the Clurichen doing when it comes into Brandonsford from the riverbanks each night?

classification.grounding_justification: Reginald's warning explicitly raises a nightly visitor up to no good without saying what it does.
classification.investigative_depth_justification: The answer would reveal a hidden nightly activity and the creature's intentions in town.
classification.narrative_payoff_justification: Learning its activity could explain mischief in town and change the party's understanding of local troubles.
classification.investigative_potential_justification: Could be pursued by watching the riverbanks at night, following the creature, or questioning townsfolk and animals.

facts.text: Kill the black dragon near Brandonsford and drag its body into town to collect Eric the Reeve's 1000 gold bounty.
George, a capable woodsman living a couple of houses from the Clumsy Fox who lost an arm to the dragon, could tell the party about his encounter; Eric says he might show up at the tavern tonight.

classification.support_basis: George is the only known person to have fought the dragon and could give firsthand details on where and how it attacked, though the party knows only what Eric relayed.

facts.text: Lady Hilda offers to join the party for pay on the dragon hunt.

classification.support_basis: A seasoned, armoured companion would strengthen the party against the dragon; details live on thread_4.

facts.text: Where did this black dragon come from, when Sir Brandon's dragon was killed and torn apart centuries ago?

classification.grounding_justification: Bentley says nothing like this has happened since Sir Brandon's dragon, Gill stresses that dragon was definitely dead and admits he doesn't know where dragons come from.
classification.investigative_depth_justification: The answer could reveal a hidden circumstance behind the dragon's appearance, but may be a simple fact.
classification.narrative_payoff_justification: Could tie the current dragon to the town's founding legend, but may be mundane.
classification.investigative_potential_justification: Town lore, George and Gill's sons are possible sources.

facts.text: A black dragon, not a big one per George, roams outside Brandonsford; it tore off George's arm, and Gill's three sons are out hunting it now.

classification.negative_outcome_clarity_justification: Maiming of those who confront it is shown by George's lost arm, though no specific next attack is established.
classification.outcome_severity_justification: Severe injury or death to individuals such as hunters.
classification.evidentiary_strength_justification: George's injury and Gill's sighting are reported by Eric and Gill.
classification.evidence_of_progression_justification: Gill's sons are actively hunting it, but the dragon avoided Gill and no pattern of attacks is described.
classification.preventability_justification: The party could kill it for the bounty, though how to find it is unknown.

facts.text: Lady Hilda, a seasoned-looking noblewoman with chain mail and a shield, offers to join the party for money for the dragon hunt; she says she cannot kill the dragon herself, and no fee has been named.

classification.support_basis: An armored, more experienced fighter would strengthen the party against the black dragon whose death earns Eric's 1000 gold, though she admits she cannot kill it alone and her price is unknown.

facts.text: Sir Phidipaldi told Lady Hilda the party would talk with Eric the Reeve and come back to her to take up her services.

classification.stake_basis: Hilda only offered her services for hire; no evidence she relies on the party returning beyond a possible paying job.

facts.text: Drop Dead Ned, a thief with a killer wasp in a jar on his necklace, offers himself and the wasp for hire at 100 gold a week, as long as he gets to kill people with the wasp. For a night of at least ten kills, he would give back 5 gold per kill if he can do what he wants with the bodies. Dr. Uriah said he would think about it.

classification.support_basis: Ned would add a willing killer and his wasp to the party, but play has not tied his hire to any want or debt, and his terms demand killing and the bodies.

facts.text: What happened to Brandonsford's restocking shipment, due a week ago, and why have no goods reached town in months?

classification.grounding_justification: Bentley states the shipment is a week overdue and hurting the whole town, Gill says nothing has come into town in months, and Wayman explicitly asks whether anyone has gone after it.
classification.investigative_depth_justification: The answer would reveal the cause of a months-long supply failure affecting the whole town, an underlying hidden circumstance.
classification.narrative_payoff_justification: Explaining why the town has been cut off would change the party's understanding of Brandonsford's troubles.
classification.investigative_potential_justification: It plausibly supports following the supply route and questioning townsfolk such as Bentley, Warwick and the Reeve.

facts.text: Dunk is weighing acquiring Farmer Gill's shabby prize mule, Shamus, which Gill suggests would let him start his own farm.
Farmer Gill offers to sell Shamus to Dunk for 100 gold.

classification.support_basis: Paying the price would secure the mule outright, but Dunk asked to trade work instead, suggesting he lacks or won't spend 100 gold.

facts.text: When Dunk asked to trade work for Shamus, Gill said the big work needed was killing the dragon outside town; no deal was agreed.
facts.uncertain_reason: Gill only named the work needed; he never explicitly agreed to give Shamus for killing the dragon.

classification.support_basis: Killing the dragon might earn Shamus without paying 100 gold, but the terms are unsettled and the task is dangerous.

facts.text: Gill says Warwick the smith displays a beautiful mithril chain shirt, probably the best in the world, which would fit a normal-sized person but not Dunk; Warwick always refuses to sell it.

classification.support_basis: Superb armor could protect a party member, but play ties it to no established want or debt, and Warwick refuses to sell it.

facts.text: Why is Warwick growing more paranoid and covering his shop in lucky charms and clovers? Gill thinks it is to keep away Ingrid the potion seller, who fancies him.

classification.grounding_justification: Gill describes Warwick's escalating paranoia and daily added charms as a noticeable oddity, offering only a speculative explanation.
classification.investigative_depth_justification: The answer would reveal a hidden cause or fear behind the smith's behavior.
classification.narrative_payoff_justification: Could be mundane (Ingrid) or tie into the town's troubles; mildly interesting as it stands.
classification.investigative_potential_justification: Visiting Warwick or Ingrid and questioning them plausibly supports following leads.

facts.text: Sir Phidipaldi agreed to help Quinn get back at Bentley, whom Quinn blames for stealing his ale at night; Quinn promised him 100 gold for that help.

classification.stake_basis: Quinn hates the Clumsy Fox, believes Bentley is stealing his stock, and offered 100 gold specifically for help getting back at him.

facts.text: Sir Phidipaldi agreed to stage a fake ale delivery at the Golden Egg: Quinn brings up bottles, they fill them with water, and Sir Phidipaldi makes a big show of coming in to deliver them, to see what happens.

classification.stake_basis: Quinn proposed the staged delivery as his plan to find out what happens to his stock and relies on Sir Phidipaldi to perform the delivery show.

facts.text: What empties or knocks over Quinn's stock every night at the Golden Egg? Quinn blames Bentley.

classification.grounding_justification: Quinn describes a conspicuous nightly anomaly of a full bar found half-empty or knocked over each morning, and the staged delivery is set up specifically to find out what happens.
classification.investigative_depth_justification: The answer reveals a hidden culprit and the circumstance behind a repeated pattern, possibly overturning Quinn's accusation.
classification.narrative_payoff_justification: Identifying the culprit would explain Quinn's ruin and could change the party's understanding of Bentley and the deal.
classification.investigative_potential_justification: It supports a stakeout, a staged bait delivery and questioning Quinn and Bentley.
